trust_decision.summary: BaseParser#process_instruction decides whether a '<?xml ...?>' declaration is accepted (only 'not at start' via @document_status, which stays nil after a prior xmldecl/PI/comment), and each accepted declaration with an encoding can re-set Source#encoding, which copies/decodes the whole unparsed buffer; the fix adds a duplicate-declaration check (@version) and strict, scanner-based declaration parsing.

landing_point.why: The advisory is about malformed XML / XML declarations; process_instruction is the only place that handles '<?xml' and it is named in the parser's main loop at lib/rexml/parsers/baseparser.rb:276-277 and :466-467.

fix_sites.entry_point: REXML::Document.new / Parsers::BaseParser#pull (and every parser wrapper) on a document starting with '<?'
same parse; attribute-value parsing refactored into parse_attribute_value_with_equal, reused by the xmldecl parser
same parse; DOCTYPE whitespace skipping switched to Source#skip_spaces
same parse; NOTATION whitespace skipping switched to Source#skip_spaces
Source#read_until('?>') used by new PI parsing; '?>' added to predefined term patterns

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All parsers (lib/rexml/parsers/treeparser.rb:10, lib/rexml/parsers/streamparser.rb:9, lib/rexml/parsers/sax2parser.rb:12, lib/rexml/parsers/pullparser.rb:41, lib/rexml/parsers/lightparser.rb:11, lib/rexml/parsers/ultralightparser.rb:10, lib/rexml/validation/relaxng.rb:47, lib/rexml/doctype.rb:101) wrap the single BaseParser; the source.rb change is a helper used by the core fix, not a separate entry point.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Weak: a solver could argue the whitespace-skip changes (skip_spaces) are cosmetic and leave them, but they are not needed to stop the duplicate-declaration DoS; there is no plausible out-of-scope module to argue away.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A single legitimate '<?xml version=... encoding=... standalone=...?>' must still switch source encoding (incl. UTF-16 normalisation), and ordinary '<?target content?>' processing instructions (including ones after the root) must keep parsing; an over-broad fix rejecting all PIs after the first event, or ignoring encoding, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: declaration with version only / version+encoding / version+standalone / all three
missing whitespace between pseudo-attributes, unknown pseudo-attributes, missing version, invalid standalone value (now rejected)
unclosed PI content with many '>' characters (read_until('?>') instead of /(.*?)\?>/ on IOSource)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: <!ELEMENT declaration still uses @source.match(/(.*?)>/um) on IOSource, the same unanchored lazy-scan-plus-refill shape the fix removed from PI parsing
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Written in the same style as the old PI code; a maintainer converting PI to read_until could easily leave doctype declarations alone.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: '%...;' external-entity reference in the internal subset uses /(%.*?;)\s*/um via IOSource.match
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same lazy regex scanning pattern in doctype parsing, untouched by the fix.

O9_family: Algorithmic-complexity DoS in XML parser (CWE-400/CWE-776): repeated XML declarations trigger repeated whole-buffer re-encoding

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby + bundler, rake test (test-unit); strscan gem

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Raise when a second '<?xml' declaration appears (e.g. set @document_status or a flag after the first xmldecl), which is essentially the published fix.

out_of_scope_notes: @document_status remains nil after a comment or non-xml PI, so an XML declaration after a leading comment/PI is accepted (lib/rexml/parsers/baseparser.rb:274-280, :751); a spec-conformance issue, not this DoS.
unverified: Repo size in MB not measured (no shell); lib/ is a few hundred KB, so tiny_repo is inferred from the library size and the test/data fixtures were not counted.

The exact quadratic mechanism (repeated Source#encoding= copying the rest of the buffer per declaration) comes from reading the code, not from a run; the advisory text itself was not available beyond the summary.
Whether the ELEMENT / '%...;' lazy-regex routes are actually super-linear on IOSource was not checked; they appear only as injection room, not as O8.
